Stated Claim / Post Context:
LDS Church joins the tech gold rush, leasing some of its ranchland for a data center

A farming subsidiary owned by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints is leasing land it owns in Texas for a large data center.

Actual Article Body:
(Google Earth) A satellite image of Triangle Ranch outside the small town of Paducah in the Texas Panhandle. Owned by a farming subsidiary of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, portions of the ranch are to be leased for construction of a large data center.

Comment

Add as Preferred Source

The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, operating through two of its farming subsidiaries, has agreed to unlock thousands of acres located in the Texas Panhandle for the construction of a large data center.

According to public documents, church-owned nonprofit Farmland Reserve would lease up to 3,710 acres of the estimated 100,000-acre portion it owns of the historic Triangle Ranch in rural Cottle County to a private outfit to build the 96-megawatt facility.

(Christopher Cherrington  |  The Salt Lake Tribune)

Just shy of “hyperscale” proportions, the center would consume as much electricity as roughly 75,000 average U.S. households.

Church-owned AgReserves, a for-profit business, is acting as the Utah-based faith’s operational agent on the ground in the Lone Star State.

Powering the proposed Texas center, developer Aetheris details in public documents, would be a 180-megawatt natural gas plant, which it also plans to construct on the leased land.

This site is protected by reCAPTCHA and the Google Privacy Policy and Terms of Service apply.

A statement from AgReserves to The Salt Lake Tribune framed the project as a natural extension of Farmland Reserve’s “long-term investment strategy,” which includes “leasing portions of its properties for agricultural, renewable energy and other compatible commercial uses.”

The same statement stressed that Aetheris represents an independent company, “not affiliated with Farmland Reserve or the church, and is responsible for the proposed project and related development activities.”

The portions of Triangle Ranch not leased to Aetheris will, it further added, continue as a working cattle ranch.

The Tribune reached out to Aetheris, which the company website says is based in Texas, for additional comment but did not receive a response.

The data center, which Aetheris has named Project Matter, is planned for an area about 15 miles east of Paducah, a town of barely 1,000 residents and Cottle County’s only incorporated municipality.

The project’s first phase, according to Aetheris’ filings with the county, would span 729 acres leased from Farmland Reserve.
